verdict.rationale: Eqvista's docs say it supports certificated (digital) shares and lists 'E-signing certificates' on the Premium plan. Its support articles cover executor signing roles and reissuing certificates after a shareholder has signed, so in-platform certificate signing is documented. Nothing explicitly documents the legal validity of those signatures or a permanent link between each certificate and its cap table entry, and e-signing appears limited to Premium. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of the certificate-to-cap-table linkage, legal-compliance details for the e-signatures, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can issue electronic share certificates that are legally signed in-platform and permanently linked to the cap table entry they represent

citations.quote: Yes, Eqvista supports both uncertificated (electronic) shares and certificated (digital or paper) shares.
